subject.title: fix: strip volatile output from exec result hash to fix no-progress detection (#93917)

question: After covering ordinary nonzero exits, should repeated exec outcomes with the same nonzero exit code and stable termination metadata count as no progress despite changing output?
rationale: The linked bug requires this behavior to stop common exit-code-1 loops, but it intentionally changes when the availability guard blocks retries.

options.title: Fingerprint nonzero exits as failures
options.body: Ignore volatile output for completed outcomes with a nonzero exit code while preserving output-sensitive progress for exit code zero.

options.title: Reclassify nonzero exits
options.body: Change the exec result contract so every nonzero normal exit becomes failed and uses the failed fingerprint.

options.title: Keep the narrower patch
options.body: Accept that ordinary nonzero command failures remain able to evade critical/global no-progress blocking.

recommendation.title: Fingerprint nonzero exits as failures
recommendation.body: Ignore volatile output for completed outcomes with a nonzero exit code while preserving output-sensitive progress for exit code zero.
